censoring.meaning: a censored onset is the look-back cap, so its window lies inside the KPI shift; the CENSORED slices are not evidence of precedence (Phase 8 F18); the UNCENSORED slices show no pre-onset excess

negative_controls.method: circular shift of the 60-min window statistic by >= 7 days (events / controls fixed)
month-stratified random pseudo-onsets from eligible controls (the primary p-value)
backward: window (end, end + 60 min] after each period vs controls (validation test, never a feature; 0 windows clipped at the grid end; not checked for other periods)
scale reference: window (T0, T0 + 60 min] inside the period
mirrored-position relocation: reversed-series window statistic read at the fixed anchors (one deterministic draw, not a null distribution; NC1 is the shift null)
all values after each T0 permuted and rescaled; every pre-T0 metric (8 window statistics, 5 x lead metrics) recomputed

phase8_integrity_checks.meaning: Phase 8 pipeline integrity checks (inputs, leakage, reproducibility); they confirm the analysis ran correctly and are not a favourable result

o2_excluded.note: own 12-period event set (post-result amendment, a second test of the same hypothesis, not multiplicity-adjusted); on the primary's own periods p is the like_for_like_p_value; WEAK and analyser-dependent; not preferred

primary_endpoint.definition: median rank excess over (T0 - 60 min, T0] vs month-matched ordinary running; T0 = Phase 6 CUSUM onset; randomisation p from month-stratified random pseudo-onsets (NC2)

data.question: Was the frozen Phase 7 risk rank elevated over (T0 - 60 min, T0] before the Phase 6 KPI-derived abnormal-period onsets, relative to month-matched ordinary running?

disclaimer: Historical validation results only. Phase 8 did not support an early-warning claim against the KPI-derived abnormal periods. Nothing here is a live warning.
